boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Case Western Reserve University
boards.description: From 24-hour study marathons at Kelvin Smith Library to midnight pizza at Rascal House, these late-night destinations define the after-hours experience for CWRU students.

cards.title: Overnight Study at KSL
cards.subtitle: The 24/5 Academic Hub
cards.notes: Access the first floor 24 hours a day from Sunday through Thursday during the regular semester for late-night research and group work.
cards.short_summary: The primary library at CWRU offers 24-hour access to its first floor for students during the academic week.
cards.evidence_claim: The first floor of Kelvin Smith Library is open for overnight study access to CWRU students with active IDs Sunday through Thursday during the regular semester.
cards.source_title: Hours | Kelvin Smith Library - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours Sunday through Thursday; requires valid CWRU ID for entry after 8:00 PM.

cards.title: Midnight Slices at Rascal House
cards.subtitle: University Circle Pizza Staple
cards.notes: Order a late-night pizza or wings at this Euclid Avenue favorite, which stays open until 2:00 AM or later most nights of the week.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing local pizza chain serving University Circle with late-night delivery and carry-out options.
cards.evidence_claim: Rascal House Pizza in University Circle is open until 2:00 AM Monday through Saturday and 1:30 AM on Sunday.
cards.source_title: Rascal House Pizza - University Circle
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM Mon-Sat and 1:30 AM Sun.

cards.title: Late Night at The Den
cards.subtitle: North Campus Dining Hub
cards.notes: Visit this North Campus diner for late-night meal swipes, featuring a menu of burgers, sandwiches, and breakfast items until 2:00 AM.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused diner on North Campus providing late-night meal options and a social atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Den (North Campus Diner) offers late-night dining services, typically operating until 2:00 AM for students on meal plans.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Locations | Dining Services - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open late night until 2:00 AM; accepts meal swipes and CaseCash.

cards.title: Warm Cookie Delivery
cards.subtitle: Uptown Dessert Run
cards.notes: Satisfy a late-night sweet tooth with warm cookies delivered to your dorm or picked up at the Uptown location until 1:00 AM.
cards.short_summary: A popular bakery specializing in late-night cookie delivery and walk-up service near the CWRU campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies in University Circle is open until 12:00 AM Sun-Wed and 1:00 AM Thu-Sat.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies - University Circle
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM on weekends; delivery available to campus dorms.

cards.title: South Campus Late Night
cards.subtitle: Fribley Dining Hall
cards.notes: Head to Fribley Commons on South Campus for late-night dining options, a convenient stop for students living in the Carlton Road area.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining hall for South Campus residents, offering extended hours for late-night meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Fribley Commons provides 'Fribley Late Night' dining services for students during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Locations | Dining Services - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours typically run until 11:00 PM or midnight depending on the semester schedule.

cards.title: Jolly Scholar Karaoke
cards.subtitle: Thwing Center Social Spot
cards.notes: Enjoy burgers and milkshakes at this on-campus restaurant, which hosts karaoke and remains open until 2:00 AM on Thursday nights.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus gastropub and brewery located in the Thwing Center that serves as a late-night social hub.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jolly Scholar is open until 2:00 AM on Thursdays and 12:00 AM on Fridays.
cards.source_title: The Jolly Scholar
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM on Thursdays; under-21 safe for dining.

cards.title: The Tink After Hours
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Student Center
cards.notes: Utilize the open lounge spaces and study areas in 'The Tink' at any hour, as the building remains accessible to students 24/7.
cards.short_summary: The central student union at CWRU, offering 24-hour access to common areas and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Tinkham Veale University Center is open 24 hours a day for student access.
cards.source_title: Visit Us | Student Centers - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; requires CWRU ID for entry during late-night hours.

cards.title: Leutner Late Night
cards.subtitle: North Campus Meal Swipes
cards.notes: Grab a late-night snack or meal at Leutner Commons, the primary dining destination for students living on the North Residential Area.
cards.short_summary: A major dining hall on North Campus that offers extended late-night hours for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Leutner Commons offers 'Late Night' dining options for students, typically operating until 10:00 PM or later.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Locations | Dining Services - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours vary by semester; check the Transact mobile app for current daily schedules.

cards.title: Uptown Ice Cream Run
cards.subtitle: Local Cleveland Favorite
cards.notes: Visit the Uptown shop for a scoop of locally-made ice cream, open until 10:30 PM daily for a post-study treat.
cards.short_summary: A beloved Cleveland ice cream parlor with a location in the heart of the Uptown district near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mitchell's Homemade Ice Cream in University Circle is open daily from 11:00 AM to 10:30 PM.
cards.source_title: Find a Shop — Mitchell's Homemade
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:30 PM every night.

cards.title: Spartie Mart Snacks
cards.subtitle: Campus Convenience Store
cards.notes: Pick up snacks, drinks, and essentials at this on-campus convenience store, which offers extended evening hours for students.
cards.short_summary: A university-run convenience store providing quick food and household items to the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Spartie Mart is a campus convenience location that accepts CaseCash and offers evening hours.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Locations | Dining Services - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Hours typically extend until 11:00 PM or midnight during the semester.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, quiet lounges, and specialized labs that Case Western students use to navigate their rigorous academic schedules.

cards.title: Decompress in the KSL Zen Zone
cards.subtitle: Kelvin Smith Library
cards.notes: Take a mental break with puzzles, games, and mindfulness activities in this dedicated wellness space on the library's first floor.
cards.short_summary: A wellness-focused relaxation area within the Kelvin Smith Library featuring mindfulness tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zen Zone is a space for wellness and relaxation containing puzzles, games, and mindfulness activities.
cards.source_title: Spaces | Kelvin Smith Library
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; accessible to students with a valid CWRU ID.

cards.entity_name: Peter B. Lewis Building Upper Floors
cards.title: Study in the Gehry-Designed Curves
cards.subtitle: Weatherhead School of Management
cards.notes: Navigate the fourth and fifth floors for quiet, sun-filled lounges and architectural nooks often overlooked by those on the lower levels.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study lounges located on the upper levels of the iconic Frank Gehry-designed business school building.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth and fifth levels of the Peter B. Lewis Building are less inhabited and feature go-to study spots like the fourth-floor lounge.
cards.source_title: Hidden gems: Places to study off the beaten path
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; primarily used by Weatherhead students but open to the campus community.

cards.title: Collaborate at the Innovation Hub
cards.subtitle: Richey Mixon Building
cards.notes: Utilize the second-floor collaboration space for group projects, featuring comfortable couches and whiteboards in a high-energy makerspace.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated collaboration and community floor within the seven-story Sears think[box] innovation center.
cards.evidence_claim: Sears think[box] is a seven-story innovation center with a community floor and collaboration spaces.
cards.source_title: Sears think[box] | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; check website for specific floor hours and training requirements.

cards.title: Find a Home Base in Thwing
cards.subtitle: Thwing Center Lower Level
cards.notes: Socialize or study in this 'home-like' lounge featuring a kitchenette, game room, and TV area specifically for commuters.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated facility for off-campus students featuring study rooms and recreational amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Off Campus Student Lounge in Thwing Center offers a living room, game room, study room, and kitchenette for students residing off campus.
cards.source_title: Off Campus Student Lounge
cards.access_notes: Requires a current CWRU ID for entry; located in the lower level of Hitchcock Hall.

cards.title: Group Study at Wade Commons
cards.subtitle: North Residential Village
cards.notes: Gather for group work in this large collaboration space equipped with tables and couches, conveniently located near North Village dining.
cards.short_summary: A popular collaboration room for North Residential Village students located within Wade Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pioneer Room inside Wade Commons offers a large collaboration space with table and couch seating.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus
cards.access_notes: Primarily serves North Residential Village students; open during Wade Commons hours.

cards.title: Unwind at The Spot
cards.subtitle: Leutner Commons Lower Level
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of Leutner for a quiet retreat with couches and tables, often used for student events and late-night studying.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student gathering and event space located in the basement of Leutner Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spot is located in the lower level of Leutner Commons and can seat up to 100 guests.
cards.source_title: The Spot | Student Centers
cards.access_notes: Open for general student use when not reserved for private events.

cards.title: Focus at the Harris Library
cards.subtitle: Mandel School, Room 175
cards.notes: Escape the main library crowds at this specialized social work library, offering a quiet environment and research assistance.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized library within the Mandel School of Applied Social Sciences.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lillian and Milford Harris Library is located in Mandel School, room 175, and provides research help and study space.
cards.source_title: Lillian and Milford Harris Library
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday until 7 PM during the fall semester; check website for seasonal hours.

cards.title: Read in the Hart Crane Room
cards.subtitle: Thwing Center
cards.notes: Enjoy a 'homey' atmosphere for evening study sessions in this cozy reading room located within the central student union.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable, living-room style reading space located in the Thwing Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hart Crane Reading Room in Thwing Center is described as a homey and cozy place to get work done.
cards.source_title: Spaces by Type | Student Centers
cards.access_notes: Open during Thwing Center operating hours; accessible to all students.

cards.title: Study at the Health Education Campus
cards.subtitle: Samson Pavilion, 4th Floor
cards.notes: Access modern lounges, kitchenettes, and lockers on the fourth floor of the Samson Pavilion, designed for health profession students.
cards.short_summary: Advanced study and lounge spaces for health sciences students located in the Samson Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Learning Communities on the fourth floor of Samson Pavilion include kitchenettes, lockers, and space to lounge and study.
cards.source_title: Dining and Study Spaces | Health Education Campus
cards.access_notes: Priority access for students in health profession programs; requires CWRU ID for entry.

cards.title: Collaborate in the Nord Atrium
cards.subtitle: Case Quad
cards.notes: Use the scattered tables in the high-ceilinged atrium for group sessions, or find a quiet classroom on the upper levels for privacy.
cards.short_summary: A central, open-air study and collaboration space located in the heart of the engineering quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Nord Hall holds various classrooms and open spaces; the atrium has scattered tables great for group study sessions.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically accessible late for students with quad building access.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and cultural experiences on and around the Case Western Reserve University campus, from world-class art galleries to peaceful botanical gardens.

cards.title: Wander the Permanent Galleries
cards.subtitle: Steps from the Tinkham Veale University Center
cards.notes: Explore over 45,000 objects for free. CWRU students also get free admission to special ticketed exhibitions by showing their university ID at the desk.
cards.short_summary: A world-class art museum with free permanent galleries and student-specific perks for special exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The CMA's permanent galleries are completely free to all members of the public; CWRU students also receive free access to all temporary exhibits with student IDs.
cards.source_title: Discovering Cleveland through museums - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday; closed Mondays. Permanent collection is free for everyone.

cards.title: Relax by the Fine Arts Garden
cards.subtitle: University Circle's central park
cards.notes: Walk the paths around the lagoon or sit on the lawn. It is a popular spot for outdoor study sessions and photography near the museum's south entrance.
cards.short_summary: A scenic public park and lagoon featuring the Fine Arts Garden and the Fountain of the Waters.
cards.evidence_claim: The land surrounding Wade Lagoon near the Cleveland Museum of Art was always intended to be a free and accessible public park.
cards.source_title: Wade Lagoon and the City Beautiful Movement | CMA Thinker
cards.access_notes: Public park accessible 24/7; best visited during daylight hours.

cards.title: Hang Out in the Tink
cards.subtitle: The 24/7 campus hub
cards.notes: Use the open lounges, study booths, or the grand staircase. The building is open to the community during the day and requires student ID for late-night entry.
cards.short_summary: The central student union at CWRU, offering 24/7 access for students and various social spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tinkham Veale University Center is open 24 hours a day; during late-night hours (10 p.m. to 7 a.m.), present your CWRU ID for access.
cards.source_title: About | Tinkham Veale University Center
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with ID; public access during standard business hours.

cards.title: Tour the Botanical Displays
cards.subtitle: Year-round indoor gardens
cards.notes: Walk through themed gardens and seasonal floral displays. Admission and parking are free for all visitors every day of the week.
cards.short_summary: A city-run greenhouse and botanical garden offering free admission to indoor and outdoor plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenhouse is free to visit, and open year-round from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm daily, including weekends and holidays.
cards.source_title: Rockefeller Park Greenhouse | City of Cleveland Ohio
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

cards.title: See Historic Medical Artifacts
cards.subtitle: Inside the Allen Memorial Medical Library
cards.notes: View rare books and medical instruments from the 1800s. The museum is free and open to the public on the third floor of the library building.
cards.short_summary: A specialized museum on campus featuring a vast collection of medical history artifacts and rare books.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Dittrick Museum of Medical History is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Dittrick Medical History Center
cards.access_notes: Open Fridays 10:30 AM - 4:00 PM and Saturdays 12:00 PM - 4:00 PM.

cards.title: Attend a Student Orchestra Concert
cards.subtitle: Free music at Silver Hall
cards.notes: Watch CWRU Department of Music performances in a restored historic temple. While tickets are free, you must register online in advance to secure a seat.
cards.short_summary: Free admission to university music department concerts held at the Maltz Performing Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Concerts are free, but registration is required; the series offers opportunities for audiences of all ages to experience inspiring live music.
cards.source_title: CWRU Music: Orchestra Concert | Maltz Performing Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Check the event calendar for specific dates; registration is required for free tickets.

cards.title: Explore the Glasshouses
cards.subtitle: Free for students via the Access Program
cards.notes: Visit the Costa Rican rainforest and Madagascar desert biomes. CWRU students get one free admission per week with their university ID.
cards.short_summary: A large botanical garden with indoor glasshouses and outdoor gardens, free for CWRU students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Free Access program allows students to visit the Cleveland Botanical Garden one time per week with a valid student ID.
cards.source_title: Free Access Program | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Student ID required for free entry; check website for seasonal hours.

cards.title: View Special Collections Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Ancient coins and university history
cards.notes: Check out rotating exhibits in the Hatch Reading Room or the central staircase. The library is open to the community for browsing and reading during designated hours.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library featuring free public exhibits and special collections displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kelvin Smith Library Special Collections Coin Collection is on view in the Henry R. Hatch Reading Room; KSL welcomes community members during designated hours.
cards.source_title: Visit Us | Kelvin Smith Library
cards.access_notes: Community visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID to enter.

cards.title: Study in the Atrium
cards.subtitle: A central Case Quad gathering spot
cards.notes: Find a table in the high-ceilinged atrium or use the lounge spaces on the upper levels. It is a reliable spot for group work or solo study between classes.
cards.short_summary: A major academic building on the Case Quad with large open spaces for student use.
cards.evidence_claim: In the atrium, scattered tables make it great for group study sessions, while sitting on the upper levels are ideal for students wanting privacy.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; card access may be required after hours.

cards.title: Walk the Cultural Gardens
cards.subtitle: A tour of global heritage
cards.notes: Stroll through over 30 gardens representing different nationalities along MLK Jr. Drive. The gardens are public, free, and located just north of campus.
cards.short_summary: A series of public gardens along Rockefeller Park celebrating Cleveland's diverse ethnic heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cleveland Cultural Gardens feature over 30 developed gardens showcasing cultural contributions; they are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Rockefeller Park Greenhouse | City of Cleveland Ohio
cards.access_notes: Public park area; accessible during daylight hours.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Discover ten distinct study environments across the Case Western Reserve University campus, from historic reading rooms to modern innovation centers.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Kelvin Smith Library, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Enter the second floor for a strictly silent environment. This space is designed for deep focus and individual work without the distraction of group discussions.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study space located on the second floor of the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Kelvin Smith Library provides a Quiet Reading Room specifically intended for quiet study.
cards.source_title: Spaces | Kelvin Smith Library - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; CWRU ID required for late-night access.

cards.title: Main Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Corner of Euclid Ave. and Adelbert Rd.
cards.notes: Study among historic portraits and chandeliers in this Classical Revival space. It offers a traditional academic atmosphere with large windows facing Euclid Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A historic, high-ceilinged reading room known for its quiet, traditional academic ambiance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Allen Memorial Medical Library features a main reading room and three large quiet study rooms.
cards.source_title: About Us | Cleveland Health Sciences Library | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Accessible via CWRU ID card; typically open 10:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays.

cards.title: Floor 6 Co-working Space
cards.subtitle: Richey Mixon Building
cards.notes: Utilize the open co-working area on the sixth floor for brainstorming and group projects. No reservation is required for the general open seating areas.
cards.short_summary: An open-access innovation and co-working floor within the seven-story makerspace.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 6 of Sears think[box] features open co-working space available for use without prior reservation.
cards.source_title: Meeting Spaces | Sears think[box] - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; check website for specific daily hours (typically 9 a.m. - 7 p.m. weekdays).

cards.title: Weatherhead Student Center
cards.subtitle: 11119 Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Find cloistered desks and secluded study spots on the upper levels of this Frank Gehry-designed building. It offers a modern, quiet alternative to the main floor lounge.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level study area located above the main entrance of the business school.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peter B. Lewis Building student center includes comfy chairs and a quieter upper area with cloistered desks.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; study rooms can be reserved by students.

cards.title: Tinkham Veale Booths
cards.subtitle: 11038 Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Use the spacious booths for a mix of social study and snack access. These spots are ideal for students who prefer a comfortable din over absolute silence.
cards.short_summary: Spacious seating booths located in the central campus hub near dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tinkham Veale University Center offers booths that are spacious and located near food options like Med-23.
cards.source_title: A letter to those interested in new study spots - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with CWRU ID; public access during daytime hours.

cards.title: Upstairs Study Area
cards.subtitle: 11440 Murray Hill Road
cards.notes: Head to the renovated upstairs seating for a quieter environment away from the main dining floor. Some rooms in this area include whiteboards for group work.
cards.short_summary: A renovated seating and study area located on the upper level of the South Side dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Fribley Commons has renovated seating upstairs that is far enough from noise for quiet work and includes whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Accessible during dining hall operating hours.

cards.title: Harris Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: 11235 Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Visit this specialized library for a quiet, focused environment. It is part of the Mandel School and offers a smaller, more intimate setting than KSL.
cards.short_summary: A quiet academic library serving the Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel School of Applied Social Sciences.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lillian and Milford Harris Library provides study spaces and is part of the Spartan Reservation System.
cards.source_title: Lillian and Milford Harris Library | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m. – 5 p.m.; closed on weekends.

cards.title: HEC Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: 9501 Euclid Avenue
cards.notes: Explore various study areas throughout the pavilion, including Student Learning Communities on the fourth floor with kitchenettes and lounge seating.
cards.short_summary: Modern study and collaboration spaces located within the Health Education Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Samson Pavilion offers a variety of study spaces, including Student Learning Communities on the fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Dining and Study Spaces | Health Education Campus | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Priority access for health profession students; CWRU ID required for entry.

cards.title: Tomlinson Quiet Lounge
cards.subtitle: Case Quad
cards.notes: Find a cozy spot in the swivel chairs on the second floor. This area is known for being quiet and convenient for students with classes on the Case Quad.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, comfortable lounge area located on the second floor of Tomlinson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of Tomlinson Hall is described as cozy and quiet, fitted with swivel chairs.
cards.source_title: A letter to those interested in new study spots - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Open during building operating hours.

cards.title: Nord Basement Lounge
cards.subtitle: 10900 Euclid Avenue
cards.notes: Relax on the sofas in the Nord Hall basement for reading or laptop work. It provides a more casual, low-light environment compared to the upper floors.
cards.short_summary: A casual lounge area with sofas located in the basement of Nord Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nord Hall basement has cozy sofas suitable for laptop work or reading.
cards.source_title: A letter to those interested in new study spots - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the corridors and micro-districts surrounding Case Western Reserve University, from the historic wood-block streets of Hessler to the vibrant Italian eateries of Little Italy.

cards.title: The Uptown District
cards.subtitle: Euclid Avenue at East 115th Street
cards.notes: Walk this modern corridor to find the university bookstore, local eateries, and the Museum of Contemporary Art Cleveland.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant residential and retail corridor serving as the university's modern 'main street.'
cards.evidence_claim: Uptown is a vibrant residential, shopping, dining, and entertainment district located on Euclid Avenue in the University Circle neighborhood.
cards.source_title: Explore the Uptown District - Cleveland - University Circle
cards.access_notes: Public street with 24/7 sidewalk access; business hours vary.

cards.title: Hessler Road Historic District
cards.subtitle: Hessler Road and Hessler Court
cards.notes: Visit Cleveland's only remaining wood-block paved street, a historic site of student activism and community preservation.
cards.short_summary: A historic residential street known for its unique wood-block paving and counterculture legacy.
cards.evidence_claim: Hessler Court is the only remaining Cleveland street to have wood block paving and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.source_title: HESSLER RD. AND HESSLER COURT HISTORIC DISTRICT | Encyclopedia of Cleveland History
cards.access_notes: Public residential street accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Little Italy Main Street
cards.subtitle: Mayfield Road Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll past historic bakeries and galleries in this century-old neighborhood adjacent to the south campus.
cards.short_summary: The primary thoroughfare of Cleveland's historic Little Italy, famous for its cultural heritage and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Little Italy was established by Italian immigrants who settled in the area that is now Mayfield and Murray Hill Roads.
cards.source_title: Explore Little Italy - University Circle
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; best explored on foot during daylight or evening dining hours.

cards.title: The Base of the Hill
cards.subtitle: Murray Hill Road
cards.notes: Find student-friendly pizza shops and the historic Holy Rosary Church at this intersection of campus and community.
cards.short_summary: A key residential and commercial street connecting the university's south campus to Little Italy.
cards.evidence_claim: Murray Hill Road is one of the two primary streets defining the historic Little Italy neighborhood.
cards.source_title: Little Italy Cleveland – A Historic Neighborhood
cards.access_notes: Public street; connects directly to the South Residential Village.

cards.title: The Museum Gateway
cards.subtitle: Ford Drive
cards.notes: Walk this block to reach the Glidden House and the entrance to the university's North Residential Village.
cards.short_summary: A scenic street bordering the campus that houses historic architecture and provides access to Wade Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Glidden House is located at 1901 Ford Drive, placing visitors in the midst of University Circle attractions.
cards.source_title: Attractions & Things To Do In University Circle - Glidden House
cards.access_notes: Public street; primary route for North Campus move-in.

cards.title: The Humanities Walk
cards.subtitle: Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Visit the Undergraduate Admission Welcome Center or explore the future site of the university's Humanities Building.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, tree-lined street on the northern edge of campus home to several university administrative and academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Undergraduate Admission Welcome Center is located at 11402 Bellflower Road.
cards.source_title: Directions and Parking | Undergraduate Admission
cards.access_notes: Public street; central to the North Residential Village.

cards.title: North Village Corridor
cards.subtitle: Juniper Road
cards.notes: Navigate this street to find first-year residence halls like Cutter and Smith in the Juniper Residential Community.
cards.short_summary: A primary residential street for first-year students living in the North Residential Village.
cards.evidence_claim: Cutter House is a traditional-style residence hall in the first-year Juniper residential community on Juniper Road.
cards.source_title: Cutter House - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Public street; often restricted to one-way traffic during move-in periods.

cards.title: The Uptown Shortcut
cards.subtitle: East 115th Street
cards.notes: Use this street as a pedestrian shortcut between the South Campus and the shops at Uptown.
cards.short_summary: A residential street that serves as a key pedestrian link between different sections of the University Circle area.
cards.evidence_claim: This section of E. 115th is often used today by students as a quick shortcut to Uptown.
cards.source_title: East 115th Street - A series on abandoned buildings in University Circle
cards.access_notes: Public street; includes the university's Sustainability House at the corner of Wade Park Ave.

cards.title: The Medical Link
cards.subtitle: Cornell Road
cards.notes: Access the university's health and counseling services or the dental research building along this busy corridor.
cards.short_summary: A critical street for the university's medical and dental programs, connecting campus to University Hospitals.
cards.evidence_claim: University Health and Counseling Services is located at 2124 Cornell Rd.
cards.source_title: University Circle and Cleveland | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Public street; high traffic area near hospital facilities.

cards.title: The Arts & Antiques District
cards.subtitle: Larchmere Boulevard
cards.notes: Explore ten blocks of independent shops, vintage stores, and bookstores just a short distance from the campus orbit.
cards.short_summary: A quirky, independent shopping district known for its 'upbeat vitality and offbeat charm.'
cards.evidence_claim: Larchmere Boulevard is ten blocks of unique shops, art and vintage stores, and restaurants.
cards.source_title: About Larchmere
cards.access_notes: Public commercial district; best visited during weekend business hours.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From a 26-mile campus relay to a physics-defying pumpkin drop, discover the rituals that define the Spartan experience at Case Western Reserve University.

cards.title: The 26-Mile Campus Sprint
cards.subtitle: A marathon-length relay race through campus
cards.notes: Runners from each class compete in a 26-mile relay to commemorate the university's 1882 move from Hudson to Cleveland.
cards.short_summary: An annual 26-mile relay race where undergraduate classes compete for bragging rights and a spot on the commemorative rock.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hudson Relays is an annual 26-mile relay through campus intended to commemorate Western Reserve College's move from Hudson, Ohio.
cards.source_title: Hudson Relays | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April; spectators can watch from various points along the campus route.

cards.title: The Ultimate Finals Break
cards.subtitle: Late-night food and games in Thwing Center
cards.notes: Take a break from finals with free food, massages, and activities held every semester before exams begin.
cards.short_summary: A massive late-night event providing students with food and stress-relief activities during the final exam period.
cards.evidence_claim: Thwing Study Over is the perfect break from studying as you prepare for finals every fall and spring semester.
cards.source_title: Thwing Study Over | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Occurs late at night during finals week; check the student activities calendar for specific hours.

cards.title: The 'Lipstick' Physics Tribute
cards.subtitle: A monument to the famous 'aether' experiment
cards.notes: Commonly called the 'lipstick fountain,' this sculpture's water symbolizes the ether waves disproved in 1887.
cards.short_summary: A landmark fountain on the Case Quad commemorating the 1887 experiment that disproved the existence of luminiferous aether.
cards.evidence_claim: The Michelson-Morley Fountain was constructed in 1973 to commemorate the 1886 experiment that disproved the theory of the 'aether.'
cards.source_title: Guess Where: Michelson-Morley Fountain | CWRU Newsroom
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors on the Case Quad; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Campus Message Board
cards.subtitle: A dedicated space for student expression
cards.notes: Student groups paint this wall near the Tinkham Veale University Center to promote events and advocacy.
cards.short_summary: A designated campus wall where student organizations can paint messages and advertisements for upcoming activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The primary purpose of the Spirit Wall is to draw attention to campus events and activities planned by student groups.
cards.source_title: Student Advocacy and Spirit Wall Policy
cards.access_notes: Visible to the public; painting is restricted to recognized student groups following university policy.

cards.title: The Physics Pumpkin Drop
cards.subtitle: Testing gravity from the roof of Strosacker Hall
cards.notes: Every Halloween, the physics department drops pumpkins frozen in liquid nitrogen to demonstrate gravity.
cards.short_summary: A Halloween tradition where physics students drop frozen pumpkins from the roof of Strosacker Hall to observe the impact.
cards.evidence_claim: Around Halloween the physics department checks gravity with the pumpkin drop off the roof of Strosacker.
cards.source_title: traditions : r/cwru
cards.access_notes: Annual event held around Halloween; open for public viewing from the quad.

cards.title: The Year-End Celebration
cards.subtitle: Inflatables, food, and live music on the quad
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the spring semester with a day of carnival games, food trucks, and a headlining concert.
cards.short_summary: A student-run festival held on the last Saturday of the spring semester featuring music and campus-wide activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Springfest, which occurs the last Saturday of the spring semester, is a student-planned event that celebrates CWRU.
cards.source_title: Springfest | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late April; open to all CWRU students.

cards.title: The Engineering Egg Drop Twist
cards.subtitle: Protecting a lightbulb from a multi-story fall
cards.notes: During Engineers Week, students design contraptions to prevent a lightbulb from breaking when dropped in the library.
cards.short_summary: A competitive event during E-Week where teams build protective housing for lightbulbs dropped from the Kelvin Smith Library balcony.
cards.evidence_claim: The WISER Lightbulb Drop allows participants to showcase engineering skills in a competition at Kelvin Smith Library.
cards.source_title: Engineers Week 2020 - Case School of Engineering
cards.access_notes: Held annually during Engineers Week in February; spectators welcome in the library atrium.

cards.title: A Mascot's Annual Bash
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the Spartan mascot
cards.notes: Join the campus community for cake and festivities to celebrate the birthday of Spartie, the CWRU mascot.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus event featuring cake and photos to celebrate the university's mascot, Spartie.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of Student Activities & Leadership supports campus events including Spartie's Birthday Party.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Events | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Tinkham Veale University Center; open to all students.

cards.title: The Gravity-Inspired Clone
cards.subtitle: A direct descendant of Isaac Newton's tree
cards.notes: Visit the tree on the Case Quad that was grafted from the original apple tree at Isaac Newton's home.
cards.short_summary: A tree on campus that is a genetic clone of the apple tree that reportedly inspired Isaac Newton's theory of gravity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newton apple tree was grafted (i.e., cloned) from the old apple tree outside Woolsthorpe Manor.
cards.source_title: Walking tour shows campus through the accomplishments of Michelson and Morley
cards.access_notes: Located on the Case Quad near the Michelson-Morley plaque; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Campus Trick-or-Treat
cards.subtitle: Halloween festivities across campus offices
cards.notes: Students visit various campus departments and offices to collect candy and meet university staff.
cards.short_summary: A Halloween tradition where students 'crawl' through campus buildings to receive treats from participating offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Traditions & Events include the CWRU Candy Crawl.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Events | Student Activities and Leadership
cards.access_notes: Held annually on or near Halloween during business hours.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Case Western Reserve University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Navigate your first days at CWRU with this sequence of essential campus stops, from orientation traditions to local University Circle landmarks.

cards.title: Kick Off Discover Week
cards.subtitle: Orientation Headquarters
cards.notes: Check in at Wolstein Hall to receive your orientation materials and meet your orientation leaders before the mandatory sessions begin.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for new student orientation check-in and resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Week is the mandatory orientation program for new students, with the orientation office located in Wolstein Hall.
cards.source_title: Discover Week — Your CWRU Orientation | Orientation and New Student Transitions
cards.access_notes: Open during business hours for orientation check-in; mandatory for all new first-year students.

cards.title: Saturday Morning Brunch
cards.subtitle: South Side Dining
cards.notes: Head to the South Residential Village for a weekend brunch. It is a primary meeting spot for students living on the south side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A major dining hall serving the South Residential Village with weekend meal service.
cards.evidence_claim: Fribley Commons is one of the two main dining halls and offers weekend hours for students.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Locations | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open for brunch and dinner on weekends; requires a meal swipe or CaseCash.

cards.title: Climb the Elephant Stairs
cards.subtitle: South Village Connection
cards.notes: Walk the oversized steps connecting Murray Hill Road to Carlton Road. It is a rite of passage for students living in the South Village.
cards.short_summary: A massive covered staircase known for its deep treads that require multiple steps per stair.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elephant Stairs connect the lower and upper levels of the South Residential Village and are a well-known campus curiosity.
cards.source_title: Myths, Mysteries and Curiosities | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor staircase connecting residential areas.

cards.title: Explore 'The Tink'
cards.subtitle: Campus Social Hub
cards.notes: Visit the student center to find the bookstore, various food options, and student organization offices in a modern, glass-walled space.
cards.short_summary: The central university center housing student services, dining, and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Tinkham Veale University Center serves as a hub for student activities, dining, and resources like the Women's Center and LGBTQ+ Center.
cards.source_title: Tinkham Veale University Center
cards.access_notes: Open daily with extended hours; accessible to all students with a CWRU ID.

cards.title: Afternoon at the Museum
cards.subtitle: World-Class Art Next Door
cards.notes: Walk across the street to explore one of the nation's top art museums. Admission to the permanent collection is always free.
cards.short_summary: A world-renowned art museum located directly adjacent to the CWRU campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cleveland Museum of Art is free to the public and is a primary cultural attraction for CWRU students.
cards.source_title: Free Access Program | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday; closed Mondays. General admission is free.

cards.title: Relax by Wade Lagoon
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Garden
cards.notes: Take a break at the scenic lagoon in front of the art museum. It is a popular spot for photos and quiet study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque lagoon and park area located between the campus and the Cleveland Museum of Art.
cards.evidence_claim: Wade Lagoon and the surrounding Fine Arts Garden are public park spaces frequently used by the CWRU community.
cards.source_title: Wade Lagoon and the City Beautiful Movement | Cleveland Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Public park accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Dinner at The Jolly
cards.subtitle: Campus Grill and Diner
cards.notes: Grab a burger or a milkshake at this on-campus eatery. It is a favorite for casual meals and accepts meal swipes for certain items.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus restaurant and bar known for its burgers and student-friendly atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jolly Scholar is an on-campus dining location that accepts meal swipes and CaseCash.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Locations | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open daily; kitchen typically closes at 10:00 PM. Under-21 safe for dining.

cards.title: Sunday Activities Fair
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Visit the KSL Oval during orientation to find student organization tables and learn how to get involved on campus.
cards.short_summary: The large green space in front of the main library, used for major campus events and fairs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Activities Fair is held on the Kelvin Smith Library Oval during orientation week.
cards.source_title: Events and Programming | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space; fair times vary by orientation schedule.

cards.title: Walk to Little Italy
cards.subtitle: Mayfield Road Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll down Mayfield Road to Cleveland's historic Little Italy for a cannoli at Presti's or dinner at a local trattoria.
cards.short_summary: A historic neighborhood adjacent to campus famous for its Italian bakeries and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Little Italy is a short walk from the first-year residence halls and is a recommended off-campus destination for new students.
cards.source_title: Your first trip off campus: Where to go | Orientation and New Student Transitions
cards.access_notes: Public neighborhood; most businesses open daily until late evening.

cards.title: Late Night Ice Cream
cards.subtitle: Uptown Treat
cards.notes: End your weekend with a scoop of locally-made ice cream at the Uptown shop. It is a staple for CWRU students and campus tours.
cards.short_summary: A popular local ice cream shop located in the Uptown district bordering campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mitchell's Ice Cream is a default ending to campus tours and a popular student hangout in the Uptown area.
cards.source_title: Your first trip off campus: Where to go | Orientation and New Student Transitions
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM on weekends.
